subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What measurement environment, scope, and acceptance criteria should #53600 use for a native-Linux reasoning-latency runbook?
rationale: The issue asks for analysis across many runtime layers, and current source already has partial telemetry primitives, so automation needs maintainer intent before deciding which layers and proof level are sufficient.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux Gateway runbook that uses existing telemetry and identifies only measured gaps as follow-up work.

options.title: Queue broad instrumentation now
options.body: Start a multi-surface instrumentation PR immediately, accepting higher review and compatibility risk across agents, memory, Telegram, and host diagnostics.

options.title: Close as already covered
options.body: Treat existing docs and OTEL as sufficient, even though they do not provide the requested layer-by-layer latency analysis.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded native-Linux Gateway runbook that uses existing telemetry and identifies only measured gaps as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is cross-cutting performance/product scope, and recent adjacent reliability work plus the current HEAD history make steipete the best available routing owner from the owner evidence.
